or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Muffet

![demo](img/demo.gif)

Muffet is a fast website link checker which scrapes and inspects all pages in a website recursively.

## Features

- Massive speed
- High compatibility with web browsers
- Different tag support (`a`, `img`, `link`, `script`, etc)
- Multiple output formats (text, JSON, and JUnit XML)

## Installation

### Go

If you have Go installed:

```sh
go install github.com/raviqqe/muffet/v2@latest
```

### Homebrew

On macOS and Linux:

```sh
brew install muffet
```

### Docker

```sh
docker pull raviqqe/muffet
```

### Command line

Check a website:

```sh
muffet https://example.com
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run raviqqe/muffet https://example.com
```

    "ignore-fragments": ("ignore_fragments", "-f, --ignore-fragments"),
    "json": ("json_alias", "--json"),
    "experimental-verbose-json": ("experimental_verbose_json", "--experimental-verbose-json"),
    "junit": ("junit_alias", "--junit"),
    "verbose": ("verbose", "-v, --verbose"),
    "skip-tls-verification": ("skip_tls_verification", "--skip-tls-verification"),
    "one-page-only": ("one_page_only", "--one-page-only"),
    "help": ("help", "-h, --help"),
    "version": ("version", "--version"),
}

SHORT_TO_LONG = {
    "b": "buffer-size",
    "c": "max-connections",
    "e": "exclude",
    "i": "include",
    "f": "ignore-fragments",
    "r": "max-redirections",
    "t": "timeout",
    "v": "verbose",
    "h": "help",
}

INT_FIELDS = {
    "buffer_size",
    "max_connections",
    "max_connections_per_host",
    "max_response_body_size",
    "max_redirections",
    "rate_limit",
    "timeout",
}
UINT_FIELDS = {"max_retries"}


def parse_int_value(value: str, alias: str, unsigned: bool = False) -> int:
    try:
        if unsigned and value.startswith("-"):
            raise ValueError
        # Go's strconv.ParseInt/ParseUint with base 10 accepts leading + or -.
        n = int(value, 10)
    except Exception:
        kind = "uint" if unsigned else "int"
        func = "ParseUint" if unsigned else "ParseInt"
        raise CLIError(
            f"invalid argument for flag `{alias}' (expected {kind}): "
            f"strconv.{func}: parsing \"{value}\": invalid syntax"
        )
    return n


def set_option(opts: Options, long_name: str, value: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    if long_name in BOOL_LONG:
        attr, _alias = BOOL_LONG[long_name]
        setattr(opts, attr, True)
        return

    attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[long_name]
    assert value is not None
    if attr in INT_FIELDS:
        setattr(opts, attr, parse_int_value(value, alias, unsigned=False))
    elif attr in UINT_FIELDS:
        setattr(opts, attr, parse_int_value(value, alias, unsigned=True))
    elif attr == "fmt":
        if value not in ("text", "json", "junit"):
            raise CLIError(
                f"Invalid value `{value}' for option `--format'. Allowed values are: text, json or junit"
            )
        opts.fmt = value
    elif attr == "color":
        if value not in ("auto", "always", "never"):
            raise CLIError(
                f"Invalid value `{value}' for option `--color'. Allowed values are: auto, always or never"
            )
        opts.color = value
    elif attr in ("excludes", "includes", "headers"):
        getattr(opts, attr).append(value)
    else:
        setattr(opts, attr, value)


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str]) -> Tuple[Options, List[str]]:
    opts = Options()
    positional: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            positional.extend(argv[i + 1 :])
            break
        if arg.startswith("--") and arg != "--":
            raw = arg[2:]
            if "=" in raw:
                name, value = raw.split("=", 1)
                has_value = True
            else:
                name, value = raw, None
                has_value = False
            if name in BOOL_LONG:
                _attr, alias = BOOL_LONG[name]
                if has_value:
                    raise CLIError(f"bool flag `{alias}' cannot have an argument")
                set_option(opts, name)
            elif name in VALUE_LONG:
                _attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[name]
                if not has_value:
                    if i + 1 >= n:
                        raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                    i += 1
                    value = argv[i]
                set_option(opts, name, value)
            else:
                raise CLIError(f"unknown flag `{name}'")
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            cluster = arg[1:]
            if not cluster:
                positional.append(arg)
            else:
                first = cluster[0]
                if first not in SHORT_TO_LONG:
                    raise CLIError(f"unknown flag `{first}'")
                first_long = SHORT_TO_LONG[first]
                # If the first short flag takes a value, the rest of the same
                # argv element is the value (with optional leading '='), just as
                # observed for -t1, -r=0, -efoo, etc.
                if first_long in VALUE_LONG:
                    _attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[first_long]
                    rest = cluster[1:]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest != "" or cluster[1:].startswith("="):
                        value = rest
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= n:
                            raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                        i += 1
                        value = argv[i]
                    set_option(opts, first_long, value)
                else:
                    j = 0
                    while j < len(cluster):
                        ch = cluster[j]
                        if ch not in SHORT_TO_LONG:
                            raise CLIError(f"unknown flag `{ch}'")
                        lname = SHORT_TO_LONG[ch]
                        if lname in BOOL_LONG:
                            set_option(opts, lname)
                            j += 1
                            continue
                        # Value flags inside a boolean cluster only consume the
                        # following argv element when they are the final char.
                        _attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[lname]
                        if j != len(cluster) - 1:
                            raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                        if i + 1 >= n:
                            raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                        i += 1
                        set_option(opts, lname, argv[i])
                        break
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    return opts, positional


class AcceptedStatus:
    def __init__(self, expr: str):
        self.exacts: set[int] = set()
        self.ranges: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        for part in expr.split(","):
            if ".." in part:
                lo_s, hi_s = part.split("..", 1)
                try:
                    lo = int(lo_s, 10)
                except Exception:
                    raise CLIError(f"invalid status code: {lo_s}")
                try:
                    hi = int(hi_s, 10)
                except Exception:
                    raise CLIError(f"invalid status code: {hi_s}")
                self.ranges.append((lo, hi))  # half-open [lo, hi)
            else:
                try:
                    code = int(part, 10)
                except Exception:
                    raise CLIError(f"invalid status code range: {part}")
                self.exacts.add(code)

    def accepts(self, status: int) -> bool:
        if status in self.exacts:
            return True
        return any(lo <= status < hi for lo, hi in self.ranges)


def translate_regex_error(pattern: str, err: re.error) -> str:
    # Match the common Go regexp diagnostics observed from the binary.
    if pattern == "" or err is None:
        return str(err)
    if "unterminated character set" in str(err):
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: `{pattern}`"
    if "missing ), unterminated subpattern" in str(err):
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing closing ): `{pattern}`"
    if "nothing to repeat" in str(err):
        # Go reports the repetition operator itself.
        op = pattern[0] if pattern else ""
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing argument to repetition operator: `{op}`"
    if "bad character range" in str(err):
        m = re.search(r"bad character range (.+?) at", str(err))
        rng = m.group(1) if m else pattern
        return f"error parsing regexp: invalid character class range: `{rng}`"
    return f"error parsing regexp: {err}: `{pattern}`"


def validate_semantics(opts: Options) -> None:
    opts.accepted_checker = AcceptedStatus(opts.accepted_status_codes)
    for pat in opts.excludes:
        try:
            opts.exclude_res.append(re.compile(pat))
        except re.error as e:
            raise CLIError(translate_regex_error(pat, e))
    for pat in opts.includes:
        try:
            opts.include_res.append(re.compile(pat))
        except re.error as e:
            raise CLIError(translate_regex_error(pat, e))
    for header in opts.headers:
        if ":" not in header:
            raise CLIError("invalid header format")
        name, value = header.split(":", 1)
        name = name.strip()
        value = value.strip()
        # The original silently ignores empty header names.
        if name:
            opts.parsed_headers.append((name, value))


HEX = set("0123456789abcdefABCDEF")


def invalid_escape(s: str) -> Optional[str]:
    i = 0
    while True:
        j = s.find("%", i)
        if j < 0:
            return None
        esc = s[j : j + 3]
        if j + 2 >= len(s) or s[j + 1] not in HEX or s[j + 2] not in HEX:
            return esc
        i = j + 3


@dataclasses.dataclass
class ParsedURL:
    display: str
    scheme: str
    host: str
    port: Optional[int]
    port_text: Optional[str]
    port_out_of_range: bool
    path: str
    query: str
    has_query_marker: bool
    fragment: str

    @property
    def netloc_no_user(self) -> str:
        if not self.host:
            return ""
        hostpart = f"[{self.host}]" if ":" in self.host and not self.host.startswith("[") else self.host
        if self.port_text is not None:
            return f"{hostpart}:{self.port_text}"
        return hostpart


def quote_path(path: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(path, safe="/%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")


def quote_query(q: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(q, safe="/?%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")


def quote_frag(f: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(f, safe="/?%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")


def _manual_host_port(netloc: str, raw_url: str) -> Tuple[str, Optional[int], Optional[str], bool, Optional[str]]:
    """Return host, port, port_text, out_of_range, parse_error."""
    # Strip userinfo for connection/display purposes.  Userinfo is rare for a
    # link checker and the observed binary does not expose it in tested docs.
    hostport = netloc.rsplit("@", 1)[-1]
    if hostport == "":
        return "", None, None, False, None
    port_text: Optional[str] = None
    host = hostport
    if hostport.startswith("["):
        end = hostport.find("]")
        if end < 0:
            return "", None, None, False, f"parse \"{raw_url}\": missing ']' in host"
        host = hostport[1:end]
        rest = hostport[end + 1 :]
        if rest.startswith(":"):
            port_text = rest[1:]
    else:
        if ":" in hostport:
            host, port_text = hostport.rsplit(":", 1)
    host_l = host.lower()
    if " " in host_l:
        return host_l, None, port_text, False, f"parse \"{raw_url}\": invalid character \" \" in host name"
    if port_text is not None:
        if port_text == "" or not port_text.isdigit():
            return host_l, None, port_text, False, f"parse \"{raw_url}\": invalid port \":{port_text}\" after host"
        port_i = int(port_text, 10)
        if port_i > 65535:
            return host_l, port_i, port_text, True, None
        return host_l, port_i, port_text, False, None
    return host_l, None, None, False, None


def canonicalize_absolute(raw_url: str, *, allow_no_host: bool = True) -> ParsedURL:
    esc = invalid_escape(raw_url)
    if esc is not None:
        raise ValueError(f"parse \"{raw_url}\": invalid URL escape \"{esc}\"")
    try:
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw_url)
    except ValueError as e:
        msg = str(e)
        if "Invalid IPv6 URL" in msg or "Invalid IPv6" in msg:
            raise ValueError(f"parse \"{raw_url}\": missing ']' in host")
        raise ValueError(f"parse \"{raw_url}\": {msg}")

    scheme = parts.scheme.lower()
    # urllib.parse.urlsplit('http://') normalizes to scheme http, empty netloc,
    # empty path.  Go's URL String for that case is "http:".
    has_query_marker = "?" in raw_url.split("#", 1)[0]
    host, port, port_text, port_oor, parse_err = _manual_host_port(parts.netloc, raw_url)
    if parse_err:
        raise ValueError(parse_err)

    path = parts.path or ("/" if parts.netloc else "")
    qpath = quote_path(path)
    qquery = quote_query(parts.query)
    qfrag = quote_frag(parts.fragment)
    netloc = ""
    if parts.netloc:
        # Keep explicit port text even if it is out of range so the later dial
        # error resembles the original.
        if host:
            hostpart = f"[{host}]" if ":" in host and not host.startswith("[") else host
            netloc = hostpart + ((":" + port_text) if port_text is not None else "")
        else:
            netloc = parts.netloc.lower()
    if scheme and netloc:
        display = f"{scheme}://{netloc}{qpath}"
    elif scheme:
        display = f"{scheme}:{qpath}"
    else:
        display = qpath
    if parts.query != "" or has_query_marker:
        display += "?" + qquery
    if parts.fragment:
        display += "#" + qfrag
    return ParsedURL(display, scheme, host, port, port_text, port_oor, qpath, qquery, has_query_marker, qfrag)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class LinkSpec:
    raw: str
    display_url: Optional[str] = None
    fetch_url: Optional[str] = None
    fragment: str = ""
    parse_error: Optional[str] = None
    skip: bool = False


SKIP_SCHEMES = {"mailto", "tel", "javascript", "data"}


def resolve_link(raw: str, base_url: str) -> LinkSpec:
    original = raw
    raw = raw.strip()
    if raw == "":
        return LinkSpec(original, skip=True)
    # Explicitly skipped schemes are ignored, as observed for mailto/tel/etc.
    low_prefix = raw.split(":", 1)[0].lower() if ":" in raw else ""
    if low_prefix in SKIP_SCHEMES or (low_prefix and low_prefix not in ("http", "https") and not raw.startswith("//")):
        return LinkSpec(original, skip=True)
    esc = invalid_escape(raw)
    if esc is not None:
        return LinkSpec(original, display_url=raw, parse_error=f"parse \"{raw}\": invalid URL escape \"{esc}\"")
    try:
        joined = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, raw)
    except Exception as e:
        return LinkSpec(original, display_url=raw, parse_error=f"parse \"{raw}\": {e}")
    try:
        p = canonicalize_absolute(joined)
    except ValueError as e:
        return LinkSpec(original, display_url=raw, parse_error=str(e))
    if p.scheme not in ("http", "https"):
        return LinkSpec(original, skip=True)
    display = p.display
    fetch = display.split("#", 1)[0]
    fragment = urllib.parse.urlsplit(display).fragment
    return LinkSpec(original, display_url=display, fetch_url=fetch, fragment=fragment)


class PageHTMLParser(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    LINK_ATTRS = {
        "a": "href",
        "img": "src",
        "link": "href",
        "script": "src",
        "iframe": "src",
        "source": "src",
        "track": "src",
    }

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.raw_links: List[str] = []
        self.ids: set[str] = set()
        self.base_href: Optional[str] = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]) -> None:
        d = {k.lower(): (v if v is not None else "") for k, v in attrs}
        if "id" in d:
            self.ids.add(d["id"])
        if "name" in d:
            self.ids.add(d["name"])
        tag_l = tag.lower()
        if tag_l == "base" and self.base_href is None and "href" in d:
            self.base_href = d["href"]
        attr = self.LINK_ATTRS.get(tag_l)
        if attr and attr in d:
            self.raw_links.append(d[attr])

    def handle_startendtag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]) -> None:
        self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)


def is_html_content_type(content_type: str) -> bool:
    return content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower() == "text/html"

    @property

class LinkResult:

class PageResult:
    url: str
    links: List[LinkResult] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)


class HTTPFetcher:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options):
        self.opts = opts
        self.cache: Dict[str, Fetched] = {}
        self.last_request = 0.0

    def fetch(self, url: str) -> Fetched:
        if url in self.cache:
            return self.cache[url]
        result = self._fetch_uncached(url)
        self.cache[url] = result
        return result

    def _fetch_uncached(self, url: str) -> Fetched:
        current = url
        redirects = 0
        last_error_url = url
        while True:
            try:
                p = canonicalize_absolute(current)
            except ValueError as e:
                return Fetched(url, current, error=str(e))
            last_error_url = p.display
            if p.scheme not in ("http", "https"):
                if p.scheme:
                    return Fetched(url, current, error=f"unsupported protocol \"{p.scheme}\". http and https are supported")
                return Fetched(url, current, error="missing port in address")
            if not p.host:
                return Fetched(url, current, error="missing port in address")
            if p.port_out_of_range and p.port_text is not None:
                hostport = f"{p.host}:{p.port_text}"
                return Fetched(url, current, error=f"error when dialing {hostport}: dial tcp: address {p.port_text}: invalid port")

            attempts = max(0, self.opts.max_retries) + 1
            response_tuple = None
            err = None
            for attempt in range(attempts):
                if self.opts.timeout < 0:
                    err = "timeout"
                    break
                try:
                    response_tuple = self._single_request(p)
                    err = None
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    err = self._format_request_error(e, p)
                    # Retry only network-ish failures, not body-limit errors.
                    if attempt + 1 >= attempts:
                        break
            if err is not None:
                return Fetched(url, last_error_url, error=err)
            assert response_tuple is not None
            status, headers, body_or_error = response_tuple
            # Redirects are handled before status-code acceptance.  Any 3xx
            # without Location is an error, even if accepted by the status set.
            if 300 <= status < 400:
                loc = headers.get("location", "")
                if not loc:
                    return Fetched(url, last_error_url, status=status, headers=headers, error="location header not set")
                if redirects >= self.opts.max_redirections:
                    return Fetched(url, last_error_url, status=status, headers=headers, error="too many redirections")
                redirects += 1
                try:
                    joined = urllib.parse.urljoin(p.display, loc)
                    cp = canonicalize_absolute(joined)
                    current = cp.display.split("#", 1)[0]
                except Exception as e:
                    return Fetched(url, last_error_url, status=status, headers=headers, error=str(e))
                continue

            if isinstance(body_or_error, str):
                return Fetched(url, last_error_url, status=status, headers=headers, error=body_or_error)
            fetched = Fetched(url, last_error_url, status=status, headers=headers, body=body_or_error)
            if fetched.is_html:
                self._parse_body(fetched)
            return fetched

    def _rate_limit(self) -> None:
        if self.opts.rate_limit and self.opts.rate_limit > 0:
            interval = 1.0 / float(self.opts.rate_limit)
            now = time.time()
            delay = self.last_request + interval - now
            if delay > 0:
                time.sleep(delay)
            self.last_request = time.time()

    def _single_request(self, p: ParsedURL) -> Tuple[int, Dict[str, str], bytes | str]:
        self._rate_limit()
        if self.opts.buffer_size < 16:
            # Approximate fasthttp's small-read-buffer failure for tiny values.
            return (
                0,
                {},
                'error when reading response headers: small read buffer. Increase ReadBufferSize. Buffer size=16, contents: "HTTP/1.0 200 OK\\r"',
            )
        port = p.port if p.port is not None else (443 if p.scheme == "https" else 80)
        timeout = self.opts.timeout if self.opts.timeout >= 0 else 0
        context = None
        if p.scheme == "https" and self.opts.skip_tls_verification:
            context = ssl._create_unverified_context()
        conn: http.client.HTTPConnection
        if self.opts.proxy:
            phost, pport = self._parse_proxy(self.opts.proxy)
            if p.scheme == "https":
                conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(phost, pport, timeout=timeout, context=context)
            else:
                conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(phost, pport, timeout=timeout)
            conn.set_tunnel(p.host, port)
        else:
            if p.scheme == "https":
                conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(p.host, port, timeout=timeout, context=context)
            else:
                conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(p.host, port, timeout=timeout)
        path = p.path or "/"
        if p.query != "" or p.has_query_marker:
            path += "?" + p.query
        try:
            conn.putrequest("GET", path, skip_host=True, skip_accept_encoding=True)
            header_names = [h[0].lower() for h in self.opts.parsed_headers]
            if "host" not in header_names:
                host_header = p.host
                explicit_port = p.port_text is not None
                if explicit_port:
                    host_header = f"{host_header}:{p.port_text}"
                conn.putheader("Host", host_header)
            for k, v in self.opts.parsed_headers:
                conn.putheader(k, v)
            if "accept" not in header_names:
                conn.putheader("Accept", "*/*")
            if "connection" not in header_names:
                conn.putheader("Connection", "close")
            conn.endheaders()
            resp = conn.getresponse()
            headers: Dict[str, str] = {}
            for k, v in resp.getheaders():
                headers[k.lower()] = v
            cl = headers.get("content-length")
            if cl is not None:
                try:
                    if int(cl) > self.opts.max_response_body_size:
                        conn.close()
                        return resp.status, headers, "body size exceeds the given limit"
                except ValueError:
                    pass
            limit = self.opts.max_response_body_size
            if limit < 0:
                data = resp.read(1)
                if data:
                    conn.close()
                    return resp.status, headers, "body size exceeds the given limit"
                return resp.status, headers, b""
            data = resp.read(limit + 1)
            conn.close()
            if len(data) > limit:
                return resp.status, headers, "body size exceeds the given limit"
            return resp.status, headers, data
        finally:
            try:
                conn.close()
            except Exception:
                pass

    def _parse_proxy(self, proxy: str) -> Tuple[str, int]:
        pr = proxy
        if "://" not in pr:
            pr = "http://" + pr
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(pr)
        host = (parts.hostname or "").lower()
        port = parts.port or 80
        return host, port

    def _format_request_error(self, e: Exception, p: ParsedURL) -> str:
        port = p.port if p.port is not None else (443 if p.scheme == "https" else 80)
        hostport = f"{p.host}:{port}"
        if isinstance(e, socket.timeout) or isinstance(e, TimeoutError):
            return "timeout"
        if isinstance(e, ConnectionRefusedError):
            return f"error when dialing {hostport}: dial tcp {hostport}: connect: connection refused"
        if isinstance(e, socket.gaierror):
            ns = first_nameserver()
            if ns:
                return f"lookup {p.host} on {ns}:53: no such host"
            return f"lookup {p.host}: no such host"
        if isinstance(e, http.client.RemoteDisconnected):
            return "the server closed connection before returning the first response byte. Make sure the server returns 'Connection: close' response header before closing the connection"
        msg = str(e)
        if "timed out" in msg.lower():
            return "timeout"
        if "Connection refused" in msg or "connection refused" in msg:
            return f"error when dialing {hostport}: dial tcp {hostport}: connect: connection refused"
        return msg or e.__class__.__name__

    def _parse_body(self, fetched: Fetched) -> None:
        try:
            text = fetched.body.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        except Exception:
            text = str(fetched.body)
        parser = PageHTMLParser()
        try:
            parser.feed(text)
        except Exception:
            # HTML parsing is forgiving in the original; ignore parser failures.
            pass
        fetched.ids = parser.ids
        base = fetched.final_url
        if parser.base_href:
            bs = resolve_link(parser.base_href, fetched.final_url)
            if not bs.skip and bs.display_url and not bs.parse_error:
                base = bs.display_url
        fetched.effective_base = base
        fetched.raw_links = parser.raw_links


def first_nameserver() -> Optional[str]:
    try:
        with open("/etc/resolv.conf", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if line.startswith("nameserver"):
                    parts = line.split()
                    if len(parts) >= 2:
                        return parts[1]
    except Exception:
        pass
    return None


class RobotsRules:
    def __init__(self, text: str):
        self.rules: List[Tuple[bool, str]] = []
        self._parse(text)

    def _parse(self, text: str) -> None:
        groups: List[Tuple[List[str], List[Tuple[bool, str]]]] = []
        agents: List[str] = []
        rules: List[Tuple[bool, str]] = []
        saw_rule = False

        def flush() -> None:
            nonlocal agents, rules, saw_rule
            if agents:
                groups.append((agents, rules))
            agents = []
            rules = []
            saw_rule = False

        for raw_line in text.splitlines():
            line = raw_line.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
            if not line or ":" not in line:
                continue
            name, value = line.split(":", 1)
            name_l = name.strip().lower()
            value = value.strip()
            if name_l == "user-agent":
                if saw_rule:
                    flush()
                agents.append(value.lower())
            elif name_l in ("disallow", "allow"):
                if not agents:
                    continue
                saw_rule = True
                if name_l == "disallow" and value == "":
                    continue
                rules.append((name_l == "allow", value))
        flush()
        specific: List[Tuple[bool, str]] = []
        star: List[Tuple[bool, str]] = []
        for ags, rs in groups:
            if any(a == "muffet" for a in ags):
                specific.extend(rs)
            elif any(a == "*" for a in ags):
                star.extend(rs)
        self.rules = specific if specific else star

    def allowed(self, url: str) -> bool:
        try:
            parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
        except Exception:
            return True
        path = parts.path or "/"
        best_len = -1
        best_allow = True
        for allow, pat in self.rules:
            if self._match(path, pat):
                l = len(pat)
                if l > best_len or (l == best_len and allow):
                    best_len = l
                    best_allow = allow
        return best_allow

    def _match(self, path: str, pat: str) -> bool:
        if "*" in pat or pat.endswith("$"):
            end_anchor = pat.endswith("$")
            body = pat[:-1] if end_anchor else pat
            regex = "^" + re.escape(body).replace("\\*", ".*") + ("$" if end_anchor else "")
            return re.search(regex, path) is not None
        return path.startswith(pat)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class RunResult:
    pages: List[PageResult]
    has_errors: bool


class Crawler:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options, root_arg: str):
        self.opts = opts
        self.root_arg = root_arg
        self.fetcher = HTTPFetcher(opts)
        self.pages: List[PageResult] = []
        self.page_map: Dict[str, PageResult] = {}
        self.visited_pages: set[str] = set()
        self.has_errors = False
        self.robots: Optional[RobotsRules] = None
        self.robots_origin: Optional[str] = None
        self.sitemap_urls: Optional[set[str]] = None

    def run(self) -> Tuple[Optional[RunResult], Optional[str]]:
        root_fetch_url, root_fragment, root_prep_error = self._prepare_root_url(self.root_arg)
        if root_prep_error:
            return None, f"failed to fetch root page: {root_prep_error}"
        assert root_fetch_url is not None
        root = self.fetcher.fetch(root_fetch_url)
        root_error = self._root_error(root, root_fragment)
        if root_error:
            return None, f"failed to fetch root page: {root_error}"
        if not root.is_html:
            return None, "root page has invalid content type"
        root_url = root.final_url.split("#", 1)[0]
        # Root final URL should be canonical and fragment-free.
        try:
            root_url = canonicalize_absolute(root_url).display.split("#", 1)[0]
        except Exception:
            pass

        if self.opts.follow_sitemap_xml:
            err = self._load_sitemap(root_url)
            if err:
                return None, err
        if self.opts.follow_robots_txt:
            err = self._load_robots(root_url)
            if err:
                return None, err

        self._enqueue_page(root_url, root)
        q_index = 0
        while q_index < len(self.pages):
            page = self.pages[q_index]
            q_index += 1
            fetched = self.fetcher.cache.get(page.url)
            if not fetched:
                continue
            self._process_page(page, fetched)
        return RunResult(self.pages, self.has_errors), None

    def _prepare_root_url(self, raw: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], str, Optional[str]]:
        esc = invalid_escape(raw)
        if esc is not None:
            return None, "", f"parse \"{raw}\": invalid URL escape \"{esc}\""
        if raw.startswith("://"):
            return None, "", f"parse \"{raw}\": missing protocol scheme"
        try:
            parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw)
        except ValueError as e:
            msg = str(e)
            if "Invalid IPv6" in msg:
                return None, "", f"parse \"{raw}\": missing ']' in host"
            return None, "", f"parse \"{raw}\": {msg}"
        if parts.scheme and parts.scheme.lower() not in ("http", "https"):
            return None, "", f"unsupported protocol \"{parts.scheme.lower()}\". http and https are supported"
        if not parts.scheme:
            return raw, "", None
        try:
            p = canonicalize_absolute(raw)
        except ValueError as e:
            return None, "", str(e)
        frag = urllib.parse.urlsplit(p.display).fragment
        return p.display.split("#", 1)[0], frag, None

    def _root_error(self, root: Fetched, root_fragment: str) -> Optional[str]:
        if root.error:
            return root.error
        assert root.status is not None
        # body-size errors are already represented as root.error.  Now check status.
        if not self.opts.accepted_checker.accepts(root.status):  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            return str(root.status)
        if root_fragment and not self.opts.ignore_fragments and root.is_html:
            decoded = urllib.parse.unquote(root_fragment)
            if decoded not in root.ids:
                return f"id #{root_fragment} not found"
        return None

    def _origin(self, url: str) -> str:
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
        return f"{p.scheme}://{p.netloc.lower()}"

    def _load_sitemap(self, root_url: str) -> Optional[str]:
        sm_url = self._origin(root_url) + "/sitemap.xml"
        sm = self.fetcher.fetch(sm_url)
        if sm.error:
            return f"failed to GET sitemap.xml: {sm.error}"
        assert sm.status is not None
        if not self.opts.accepted_checker.accepts(sm.status):  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            return f"failed to GET sitemap.xml: {sm.status}"
        text = sm.body.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        urls: set[str] = set()
        # Collect <loc> values that appear within <url> blocks; sitemap index
        # entries are intentionally not treated as pages.
        for m in re.finditer(r"<url\b[^>]*>(.*?)</url>", text, flags=re.I | re.S):
            block = m.group(1)
            lm = re.search(r"<loc\b[^>]*>(.*?)</loc>", block, flags=re.I | re.S)
            if not lm:
                continue
            loc = html_module.unescape(re.sub(r"\s+", "", lm.group(1).strip()))
            try:
                cp = canonicalize_absolute(loc)
                if cp.scheme in ("http", "https"):
                    urls.add(cp.display.split("#", 1)[0])
            except Exception:
                pass
        self.sitemap_urls = urls
        return None

    def _load_robots(self, root_url: str) -> Optional[str]:
        self.robots_origin = self._origin(root_url)
        rb_url = self.robots_origin + "/robots.txt"
        rb = self.fetcher.fetch(rb_url)
        if rb.error:
            return f"failed to fetch robots.txt: {rb.error}"
        assert rb.status is not None
        if not self.opts.accepted_checker.accepts(rb.status):  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            return f"failed to fetch robots.txt: {rb.status}"
        self.robots = RobotsRules(rb.body.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        return None

    def _enqueue_page(self, url: str, fetched: Fetched) -> None:
        final = fetched.final_url.split("#", 1)[0]
        try:
            final = canonicalize_absolute(final).display.split("#", 1)[0]
        except Exception:
            pass
        if final in self.visited_pages:
            return
        self.visited_pages.add(final)
        # Store under final URL for cache lookups as well.
        self.fetcher.cache.setdefault(final, fetched)
        page = PageResult(final)
        self.page_map[final] = page
        self.pages.append(page)

    def _process_page(self, page: PageResult, fetched: Fetched) -> None:
        base = fetched.effective_base or fetched.final_url
        seen: set[str] = set()
        specs: List[LinkSpec] = []
        for raw in fetched.raw_links:
            spec = resolve_link(raw, base)
            if spec.skip:
                continue
            key = spec.display_url if spec.display_url is not None else (spec.raw + "\0" + (spec.parse_error or ""))
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            if spec.display_url and not self._included(spec.display_url):
                continue
            specs.append(spec)

        for spec in specs:
            lr = self._check_link(spec)
            if lr is None:
                continue
            page.links.append(lr)
            if not lr.ok:
                self.has_errors = True
            if lr.ok and not self.opts.one_page_only and lr.final_url:
                fetched_target = self.fetcher.cache.get(lr.final_url) or self.fetcher.cache.get(spec.fetch_url or "")
                if not fetched_target:
                    continue
                if not fetched_target.is_html:
                    continue
                if fetched_target.status is None or not self.opts.accepted_checker.accepts(fetched_target.status):  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                    continue
                final_page = fetched_target.final_url.split("#", 1)[0]
                try:
                    final_page = canonicalize_absolute(final_page).display.split("#", 1)[0]
                except Exception:
                    pass
                if self._can_scrape(final_page):
                    self._enqueue_page(final_page, fetched_target)

    def _included(self, url: str) -> bool:
        if self.opts.include_res and not any(r.search(url) for r in self.opts.include_res):
            return False
        if self.opts.exclude_res and any(r.search(url) for r in self.opts.exclude_res):
            return False
        return True

    def _check_link(self, spec: LinkSpec) -> Optional[LinkResult]:
        if spec.parse_error:
            return LinkResult(spec.display_url or spec.raw, error=spec.parse_error)
        if not spec.fetch_url or not spec.display_url:
            return None
        fetched = self.fetcher.fetch(spec.fetch_url)
        if fetched.error:
            return LinkResult(spec.display_url, error=fetched.error)
        assert fetched.status is not None
        if not self.opts.accepted_checker.accepts(fetched.status):  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            return LinkResult(spec.display_url, error=str(fetched.status), final_url=fetched.final_url.split("#", 1)[0])
        if spec.fragment and not self.opts.ignore_fragments and fetched.is_html:
            decoded = urllib.parse.unquote(spec.fragment)
            if decoded not in fetched.ids:
                return LinkResult(spec.display_url, error=f"id #{spec.fragment} not found", final_url=fetched.final_url.split("#", 1)[0])
        final = fetched.final_url.split("#", 1)[0]
        try:
            final = canonicalize_absolute(final).display.split("#", 1)[0]
        except Exception:
            pass
        # Ensure final URL is also a cache key, since redirects are displayed
        # under their destination page when recursively scraped.
        self.fetcher.cache.setdefault(final, fetched)
        return LinkResult(spec.display_url, status=fetched.status, final_url=final)

    def _can_scrape(self, url: str) -> bool:
        if self.sitemap_urls is not None and url not in self.sitemap_urls and url not in self.page_map:
            # The root page is already in page_map.  Other pages must be listed.
            return False
        if self.robots and self.robots_origin and self._origin(url) == self.robots_origin:
            return self.robots.allowed(url)
        return True


def ordered_links(links: List[LinkResult], verbose: bool) -> List[LinkResult]:
    if verbose:
        return [l for l in links if l.ok] + [l for l in links if not l.ok]
    return [l for l in links if not l.ok]


def emit_text(result: RunResult, opts: Options) -> None:
    use_color = opts.color == "always" or (opts.color == "auto" and sys.stdout.isatty())

    def c(text: str, code: str) -> str:
        if not use_color:
            return text
        return f"\033[{code}m{text}\033[0m"

    out: List[str] = []
    for page in result.pages:
        selected = ordered_links(page.links, opts.verbose)
        if not selected and not opts.verbose:
            continue
        out.append(c(page.url, "33") + "\n")
        for link in selected:
            if link.ok:
                left = c(str(link.status), "32")
            else:
                left = c(link.error or "", "31")
            out.append(f"\t{left}\t{link.url}\n")
    sys.stdout.write("".join(out))


def go_json_dumps(obj: object) -> str:
    s = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    # Go's encoding/json escapes HTML-sensitive characters by default.
    return s.replace("&", "\\u0026").replace("<", "\\u003c").replace(">", "\\u003e")


def emit_json(result: RunResult, opts: Options) -> None:
    verbose_json = opts.verbose or (opts.json_alias and opts.experimental_verbose_json)
    arr = []
    for page in result.pages:
        links = ordered_links(page.links, verbose_json)
        if not verbose_json:
            links = [l for l in links if not l.ok]
            if not links:
                continue
        pobj = {"url": page.url, "links": []}
        for l in links:
            if l.ok:
                pobj["links"].append({"url": l.url, "status": l.status})
            else:
                pobj["links"].append({"url": l.url, "error": l.error})
        arr.append(pobj)
    sys.stdout.write(go_json_dumps(arr) + "\n")


def xml_attr(s: str) -> str:
    return xml.sax.saxutils.escape(s, {"\"": """})


def emit_junit(result: RunResult, opts: Options) -> None:
    out: List[str] = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n', "<testsuites>\n"]
    for page in result.pages:
        links = ordered_links(page.links, True)
        failures = sum(1 for l in links if not l.ok)
        if not links:
            out.append(f'  <testsuite name="{xml_attr(page.url)}" tests="0" failures="0" skipped="0"></testsuite>\n')
            continue
        out.append(
            f'  <testsuite name="{xml_attr(page.url)}" tests="{len(links)}" failures="{failures}" skipped="0">\n'
        )
        for l in links:
            out.append(f'    <testcase name="{xml_attr(l.url)}" classname="{xml_attr(page.url)}">')
            if l.ok:
                out.append("</testcase>\n")
            else:
                out.append("\n")
                out.append(f'      <failure message="{xml_attr(l.error or "")}"></failure>\n')
                out.append("    </testcase>\n")
        out.append("  </testsuite>\n")
    out.append("</testsuites>\n")
    sys.stdout.write("".join(out))


def effective_format(opts: Options) -> str:
    if opts.json_alias:
        return "json"
    if opts.junit_alias:
        return "junit"
    return opts.fmt


def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    try:
        opts, positional = parse_args(argv)
    except CLIError as e:
        print(str(e), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if opts.help:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
        return 0
    if opts.version:
        print(VERSION)
        return 0

    if len(positional) != 1:
        print("invalid number of arguments", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    try:
        validate_semantics(opts)
    except CLIError as e:
        print(str(e), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    # Approximate the observed Go panic for negative semaphore sizes.
    if opts.max_connections < 0 or opts.max_connections_per_host < 0:
        print("panic: makechan: size out of range", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    crawler = Crawler(opts, positional[0])
    result, fatal = crawler.run()
    if fatal:
        print(fatal, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    assert result is not None
    fmt = effective_format(opts)
    if fmt == "json":
        emit_json(result, opts)
    elif fmt == "junit":
        emit_junit(result, opts)
    else:
        emit_text(result, opts)
    return 1 if result.has_errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

def parse_int_value(value: str, alias: str, unsigned: bool = False) -> int:

        n = int(value, 10)
    except Exception:
        kind = "uint" if unsigned else "int"
        func = "ParseUint" if unsigned else "ParseInt"
        raise CLIError(
            f"invalid argument for flag `{alias}' (expected {kind}): "
            f"strconv.{func}: parsing \"{value}\": invalid syntax"
        )
    return n


def set_option(opts: Options, long_name: str, value: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    if long_name in BOOL_LONG:
        attr, _alias = BOOL_LONG[long_name]
        setattr(opts, attr, True)
        return

    attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[long_name]
    assert value is not None
    if attr in INT_FIELDS:
        setattr(opts, attr, parse_int_value(value, alias, unsigned=False))
    elif attr in UINT_FIELDS:
        setattr(opts, attr, parse_int_value(value, alias, unsigned=True))
    elif attr == "fmt":
        if value not in ("text", "json", "junit"):
            raise CLIError(
                f"Invalid value `{value}' for option `--format'. Allowed values are: text, json or junit"
            )
        opts.fmt = value
    elif attr == "color":
        if value not in ("auto", "always", "never"):
            raise CLIError(
                f"Invalid value `{value}' for option `--color'. Allowed values are: auto, always or never"
            )
        opts.color = value
    elif attr in ("excludes", "includes", "headers"):
        getattr(opts, attr).append(value)
    else:
        setattr(opts, attr, value)


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str]) -> Tuple[Options, List[str]]:
    opts = Options()
    positional: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            positional.extend(argv[i + 1 :])
            break
        if arg.startswith("--") and arg != "--":
            raw = arg[2:]
            if "=" in raw:
                name, value = raw.split("=", 1)
                has_value = True
            else:
                name, value = raw, None
                has_value = False
            if name in BOOL_LONG:
                _attr, alias = BOOL_LONG[name]
                if has_value:
                    raise CLIError(f"bool flag `{alias}' cannot have an argument")
                set_option(opts, name)
            elif name in VALUE_LONG:
                _attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[name]
                if not has_value:
                    if i + 1 >= n:
                        raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                    i += 1
                    value = argv[i]
                set_option(opts, name, value)
            else:
                raise CLIError(f"unknown flag `{name}'")
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            cluster = arg[1:]
            if not cluster:
                positional.append(arg)
            else:
                first = cluster[0]
                if first not in SHORT_TO_LONG:
                    raise CLIError(f"unknown flag `{first}'")
                first_long = SHORT_TO_LONG[first]
                # If the first short flag takes a value, the rest of the same
                # argv element is the value (with optional leading '='), just as
                # observed for -t1, -r=0, -efoo, etc.
                if first_long in VALUE_LONG:
                    _attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[first_long]
                    rest = cluster[1:]
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        rest = rest[1:]
                    if rest != "" or cluster[1:].startswith("="):
                        value = rest
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= n:
                            raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                        i += 1
                        value = argv[i]
                    set_option(opts, first_long, value)
                else:
                    j = 0
                    while j < len(cluster):
                        ch = cluster[j]
                        if ch not in SHORT_TO_LONG:
                            raise CLIError(f"unknown flag `{ch}'")
                        lname = SHORT_TO_LONG[ch]
                        if lname in BOOL_LONG:
                            set_option(opts, lname)
                            j += 1
                            continue
                        # Value flags inside a boolean cluster only consume the
                        # following argv element when they are the final char.
                        _attr, alias = VALUE_LONG[lname]
                        if j != len(cluster) - 1:
                            raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                        if i + 1 >= n:
                            raise CLIError(f"expected argument for flag `{alias}'")
                        i += 1
                        set_option(opts, lname, argv[i])
                        break
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    return opts, positional


class AcceptedStatus:
    def __init__(self, expr: str):
        self.exacts: set[int] = set()
        self.ranges: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        for part in expr.split(","):
            if ".." in part:
                lo_s, hi_s = part.split("..", 1)
                try:
                    lo = int(lo_s, 10)
                except Exception:
                    raise CLIError(f"invalid status code: {lo_s}")
                try:
                    hi = int(hi_s, 10)
                except Exception:
                    raise CLIError(f"invalid status code: {hi_s}")
                self.ranges.append((lo, hi))  # half-open [lo, hi)
            else:
                try:
                    code = int(part, 10)
                except Exception:
                    raise CLIError(f"invalid status code range: {part}")
                self.exacts.add(code)

    def accepts(self, status: int) -> bool:
        if status in self.exacts:
            return True
        return any(lo <= status < hi for lo, hi in self.ranges)


def translate_regex_error(pattern: str, err: re.error) -> str:
    # Match the common Go regexp diagnostics observed from the binary.
    if pattern == "" or err is None:
        return str(err)
    if "unterminated character set" in str(err):
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: `{pattern}`"
    if "missing ), unterminated subpattern" in str(err):
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing closing ): `{pattern}`"
    if "nothing to repeat" in str(err):
        # Go reports the repetition operator itself.
        op = pattern[0] if pattern else ""
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing argument to repetition operator: `{op}`"
    if "bad character range" in str(err):
        m = re.search(r"bad character range (.+?) at", str(err))
        rng = m.group(1) if m else pattern
        return f"error parsing regexp: invalid character class range: `{rng}`"
    return f"error parsing regexp: {err}: `{pattern}`"


def validate_semantics(opts: Options) -> None:
    opts.accepted_checker = AcceptedStatus(opts.accepted_status_codes)
    for pat in opts.excludes:
        try:
            opts.exclude_res.append(re.compile(pat))
        except re.error as e:
            raise CLIError(translate_regex_error(pat, e))
    for pat in opts.includes:
        try:
            opts.include_res.append(re.compile(pat))
        except re.error as e:
            raise CLIError(translate_regex_error(pat, e))
    for header in opts.headers:
        if ":" not in header:
            raise CLIError("invalid header format")
        name, value = header.split(":", 1)
        name = name.strip()
        value = value.strip()
        # The original silently ignores empty header names.
        if name:
            opts.parsed_headers.append((name, value))


HEX = set("0123456789abcdefABCDEF")


def invalid_escape(s: str) -> Optional[str]:
    i = 0
    while True:
        j = s.find("%", i)
        if j < 0:
            return None
        esc = s[j : j + 3]
        if j + 2 >= len(s) or s[j + 1] not in HEX or s[j + 2] not in HEX:
            return esc
        i = j + 3


@dataclasses.dataclass
class ParsedURL:
    display: str
    scheme: str
    host: str
    port: Optional[int]
    port_text: Optional[str]
    port_out_of_range: bool
    path: str
    query: str
    has_query_marker: bool
    fragment: str

    @property
    def netloc_no_user(self) -> str:
        if not self.host:
            return ""
        hostpart = f"[{self.host}]" if ":" in self.host and not self.host.startswith("[") else self.host
        if self.port_text is not None:
            return f"{hostpart}:{self.port_text}"
        return hostpart


def quote_path(path: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(path, safe="/%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")


def quote_query(q: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(q, safe="/?%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")


def quote_frag(f: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(f, safe="/?%:@!$&'()*+,;=-._~")


def _manual_host_port(netloc: str, raw_url: str) -> Tuple[str, Optional[int], Optional[str], bool, Optional[str]]:
    """Return host, port, port_text, out_of_range, parse_error."""
    # Strip userinfo for connection/display purposes.  Userinfo is rare for a
    # link checker and the observed binary does not expose it in tested docs.
    hostport = netloc.rsplit("@", 1)[-1]
    if hostport == "":
        return "", None, None, False, None
    port_text: Optional[str] = None
    host = hostport
    if hostport.startswith("["):
        end = hostport.find("]")
        if end < 0:
            return "", None, None, False, f"parse \"{raw_url}\": missing ']' in host"
        host = hostport[1:end]
        rest = hostport[end + 1 :]
        if rest.startswith(":"):
            port_text = rest[1:]
    else:
        if ":" in hostport:
            host, port_text = hostport.rsplit(":", 1)
    host_l = host.lower()
    if " " in host_l:
        return host_l, None, port_text, False, f"parse \"{raw_url}\": invalid character \" \" in host name"
    if port_text is not None:
        if port_text == "" or not port_text.isdigit():
            return host_l, None, port_text, False, f"parse \"{raw_url}\": invalid port \":{port_text}\" after host"
        port_i = int(port_text, 10)
        if port_i > 65535:
            return host_l, port_i, port_text, True, None
        return host_l, port_i, port_text, False, None
    return host_l, None, None, False, None


def canonicalize_absolute(raw_url: str, *, allow_no_host: bool = True) -> ParsedURL:
    esc = invalid_escape(raw_url)
    if esc is not None:
        raise ValueError(f"parse \"{raw_url}\": invalid URL escape \"{esc}\"")
    try:
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw_url)
    except ValueError as e:
        msg = str(e)
        if "Invalid IPv6 URL" in msg or "Invalid IPv6" in msg:
            raise ValueError(f"parse \"{raw_url}\": missing ']' in host")
        raise ValueError(f"parse \"{raw_url}\": {msg}")

    scheme = parts.scheme.lower()
    # urllib.parse.urlsplit('http://') normalizes to scheme http, empty netloc,
    # empty path.  Go's URL String for that case is "http:".
    has_query_marker = "?" in raw_url.split("#", 1)[0]
    host, port, port_text, port_oor, parse_err = _manual_host_port(parts.netloc, raw_url)
    if parse_err:
        raise ValueError(parse_err)

    path = parts.path or ("/" if parts.netloc else "")
    qpath = quote_path(path)
    qquery = quote_query(parts.query)
    qfrag = quote_frag(parts.fragment)
    netloc = ""
    if parts.netloc:
        # Keep explicit port text even if it is out of range so the later dial
        # error resembles the original.
        if host:
            hostpart = f"[{host}]" if ":" in host and not host.startswith("[") else host
            netloc = hostpart + ((":" + port_text) if port_text is not None else "")
        else:
            netloc = parts.netloc.lower()
    if scheme and netloc:
        display = f"{scheme}://{netloc}{qpath}"
    elif scheme:
        display = f"{scheme}:{qpath}"
    else:
        display = qpath
    if parts.query != "" or has_query_marker:
        display += "?" + qquery
    if parts.fragment:
        display += "#" + qfrag
    return ParsedURL(display, scheme, host, port, port_text, port_oor, qpath, qquery, has_query_marker, qfrag)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class LinkSpec:
    raw: str
    display_url: Optional[str] = None
    fetch_url: Optional[str] = None
    fragment: str = ""
    parse_error: Optional[str] = None
    skip: bool = False


SKIP_SCHEMES = {"mailto", "tel", "javascript", "data"}


def resolve_link(raw: str, base_url: str) -> LinkSpec:
    original = raw
    raw = raw.strip()
    if raw == "":
        return LinkSpec(original, skip=True)
    # Explicitly skipped schemes are ignored, as observed for mailto/tel/etc.
    low_prefix = raw.split(":", 1)[0].lower() if ":" in raw else ""
    if low_prefix in SKIP_SCHEMES or (low_prefix and low_prefix not in ("http", "https") and not raw.startswith("//")):
        return LinkSpec(original, skip=True)
    esc = invalid_escape(raw)
    if esc is not None:
        return LinkSpec(original, display_url=raw, parse_error=f"parse \"{raw}\": invalid URL escape \"{esc}\"")
    try:
        joined = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, raw)
    except Exception as e:
        return LinkSpec(original, display_url=raw, parse_error=f"parse \"{raw}\": {e}")
    try:
        p = canonicalize_absolute(joined)
    except ValueError as e:
        return LinkSpec(original, display_url=raw, parse_error=str(e))
    if p.scheme not in ("http", "https"):
        return LinkSpec(original, skip=True)
    display = p.display
    fetch = display.split("#", 1)[0]
    fragment = urllib.parse.urlsplit(display).fragment
    return LinkSpec(original, display_url=display, fetch_url=fetch, fragment=fragment)


class PageHTMLParser(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    LINK_ATTRS = {
        "a": "href",
        "img": "src",
        "link": "href",
        "script": "src",
        "iframe": "src",
        "source": "src",
        "track": "src",
    }

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.raw_links: List[str] = []
        self.ids: set[str] = set()
        self.base_href: Optional[str] = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]) -> None:
        d = {k.lower(): (v if v is not None else "") for k, v in attrs}
        if "id" in d:
            self.ids.add(d["id"])
        if "name" in d:
            self.ids.add(d["name"])
        tag_l = tag.lower()
        if tag_l == "base" and self.base_href is None and "href" in d:
            self.base_href = d["href"]
        attr = self.LINK_ATTRS.get(tag_l)
        if attr and attr in d:
            self.raw_links.append(d[attr])

    def handle_startendtag(self, tag: str, attrs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]]) -> None:
        self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)


def is_html_content_type(content_type: str) -> bool:
    return content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower() == "text/html"


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Fetched:
    requested_url: str
    final_url: str
    status: Optional[int] = None
    headers: Dict[str, str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
    body: bytes = b""
    error: Optional[str] = None
    ids: set[str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=set)
    raw_links: List[str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
    effective_base: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def content_type(self) -> str:
        return self.headers.get("content-type", "")

    @property
    def is_html(self) -> bool:
        return is_html_content_type(self.content_type)

class LinkResult:
    url: str
    status: Optional[int] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None

    @property
